card_title: I Have a Plan for the Whole Earth
description: God has a plan for the whole earth, and it includes judgment. We have edited Him down to the parts we like. But He is both love and justice.
excerpt: We have almost skipped that part of who He is. God is loving and God is just. God is kind and God brings judgment. Both are true. Both are Him.
verse: "I have a plan for the whole earth, a hand of judgment upon all the nations."
body_html:
This verse is a good reminder.

God has a plan for the whole earth. Not just for one nation. Not just for one people group. Not just for the parts of history we like to focus on. The whole earth. Every nation. Every era. Every kingdom that has ever risen and every one that will ever fall. All of it is under His hand.

That is the part we love to talk about. God is over everything. God is sovereign. God is in control.

But the second half of the verse is not one we love to talk about as much.

A hand of judgment upon all the nations.

We sing songs about God being good. And He is. We sing songs about God being kind. And He is. We sing songs about His love and His mercy and His faithfulness and His grace. And every bit of it is true.

But we do not sing many songs about His judgment.

We have almost skipped that part of who He is. And it is a part. A real part. Woven all through Scripture from Genesis to Revelation. God is loving and God is just. God is kind and God brings judgment. Both are true. Both are Him.

The Bible does not shy away from that. God's judgment on the nations shows up over and over. On Egypt. On Babylon. On Assyria. On Nineveh. On Israel and Judah themselves when they turned from Him. And it will show up again at the end. Revelation is not shy about it either.

We have somehow made God safe in our modern culture. We have edited Him down to the parts we like. The comforting parts. The encouraging parts. The parts that fit on a coffee mug. And we have quietly ignored the parts that make us uncomfortable.

But God is not one or the other. He is both.

If He were only love without justice, He would not be trustworthy. Evil would go unanswered. Wickedness would never be dealt with. Innocent blood would cry out forever with no response. That is not a good God. That is a passive one.

A truly good God has to deal with evil. And He does. In His timing. On His terms. According to His plan.

I think we forget how weighty that is. And I think we forget how much comfort there actually is in it. Because if God is going to bring judgment on the nations, then no wicked ruler gets away with anything forever. No injustice is truly buried. No lie stays hidden. Every hidden thing will come out in the light one day, and God will make it right.

That is not scary if you are His.

But it is a reason to make sure you actually are.

Because loving God means embracing all of Him. Not just the parts that make us feel good. The whole picture. His love, His grace, His mercy, and also His justice, His holiness, and His judgment.

He is coming back. And He is coming as both Savior and Judge.

Are you living like both are true?
question: Are you living like both are true?
